symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes accompanied by delusions and/or hallucinations that occur exclusively during the depressive episode. The psychotic content is typically mood-congruent (e.g., themes of guilt, worthlessness, illness, or deserved punishment) but can also be mood-incongruent, and it is not better explained by a primary psychotic disorder such as schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. The condition is usually severe, associated with marked functional impairment, and carries a heightened risk of suicide and hospitalization. Clinically, it is distinguished from non-psychotic depression by the presence of fixed false beliefs or perceptual disturbances and from bipolar depression by the absence of a history of manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.personality: Gina is an analytical yet creative young engineering manager who balances data-driven structure with spontaneous, people-focused leadership and a rich set of hobbies.
patient.stressor: Gina’s difficulties began after she was rapidly promoted to manage a high-visibility engineering project shortly after graduating, taking on responsibility for a team older and more experienced than she was. Initially energized, she started working longer hours, sacrificing sleep, social time, and her usual grounding routines like running and gardening as deadlines slipped and senior leadership increased pressure. Over several months, a cascade of failed milestones, critical performance feedback, and a public presentation where she felt she had let her team down eroded her confidence and led her to withdraw from friends and hobbies, while she became increasingly preoccupied with the idea that she was fundamentally incompetent and damaging the company. As the year wore on, her functioning deteriorated at work and at home to the point that she was missing meetings, avoiding decisions, and privately reacting to experiences that frightened her, prompting a concerned coworker and her manager to insist she see a psychiatrist when she confided that her perceptions no longer felt trustworthy.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep seeing and hearing things that I know shouldn’t be there, and it’s starting to scare me.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: No matter how many times people at work tell me it's 'just a project,' I'm convinced I’ve single-handedly ruined the company’s reputation and that there are probably conversations happening in the background about suing me or making an example out of me for what I’ve done.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: At the office and sometimes even at home, I hear this low, male voice muttering things like 'fraud' and 'you did this' right behind me, and I’ll catch these shadowy figures standing in the doorway or at the edge of the conference room, watching me, but when I turn fully to look, there’s nobody there and everyone else acts like nothing happened.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to unwind by going for long runs or fussing over my little balcony garden, but for months now even the thought of lacing up my shoes or watering the plants just makes me feel tired and numb, like there’s no point because I don’t deserve to enjoy anything.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Most of the time I move and talk like I’m wading through molasses—my coworkers comment that I ‘seem slowed down’—but then I’ll have these stretches, especially late at night, where I can’t sit still and just pace my tiny apartment, rubbing my hands together or picking at my skin because I feel this awful, restless dread in my body.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I constantly feel like I’m fundamentally broken and poisonous to other people, and I spend hours replaying every mistake I’ve ever made at work or with friends, genuinely believing that the project delays, my team’s stress, and even my parents worrying about me are all my fault and that I should be punished for it.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: Where I used to juggle complex engineering problems in my head, now I stare at a simple email draft or a sprint plan for twenty minutes unable to decide on a sentence or a priority, and my mind just feels foggy and blank, like I’ve lost the ability to think straight.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Pretty much every day I catch myself thinking that everyone would be better off if I just disappeared, and I’ve gone as far as looking up bridges and calculating how long it would take someone to find me, even though actually going through with it still scares me.
